turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Thank you. Well, I came in because... I just keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. I notice it a lot in photos, and especially under the bright lights at the store where I work. Even when other people tell me they don't see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. It's just been really bothering me lately.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a persistent preoccupation with a perceived tiny uneven spot on their face that others do not notice, believing it is highly visible to customers and managers.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself frequently checking that spot in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. On my breaks at work, I usually end up going to the bathroom just to check my face in the mirror. I'll spend time fixing my hair around it, trying to see if I can make it less noticeable. And I guess I also catch myself comparing my face to the girls who come through my checkout line. Sometimes I get so caught up looking in the mirror and messing with my hair that I take too long, and I actually end up being late getting back to the register.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors related to appearance concerns, specifically checking her face in the mirror, camouflaging the spot with her hair, and comparing herself to others.

turns.doctor_question: Apart from your concerns about this spot on your face, do you feel anxious in social situations for other reasons, like worrying you might say or do something embarrassing?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't worry about saying the wrong thing or embarrassing myself like that. I'm usually pretty okay talking to the customers and everything. It's really just... just the thing with my face that makes me uncomfortable when people are looking at me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reiterates that their discomfort around others is solely due to concerns about a perceived flaw on their face.

turns.doctor_question: Besides concerns about your appearance, do you experience repetitive thoughts or routines about other things, like fears of contamination, checking locks, or needing things arranged in a specific way?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really have anything like that. I don't worry about germs or checking the door or anything. It's really just the thing with my face that I get stuck on.
